correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier diagonalization of a 2x2 circulant convolution gives F_w(a)=[lB/(a+l)+w log(a+d)]/2 on a=s^2 in [0,1]. The continuously extended secant ratio tau has derivative sign T and T_prime=(1-a)(a+2d-l)/[(1+l)(a+d)^2]; this proves tau has no interior minima. If tau(0)<tau(1), comparing F_w with F_w(1) yields the sharp jump w0. Comparing F_w with F_w0 and F_w0(0) proves strict unique full blur for every w>w0. Differentiating gives a quadratic sign pattern with exactly one interior maximum in the metastable interval. M(d)=(1+d)log(1+1/d) is strictly decreasing, proving existence/uniqueness of d*. The delivered standalone checker passed 4556 finite supplementary assertions, not used as an infinite proof.

evidence: The arXiv:2611.04846v1 authors state in the abstract and Section 3.1 that they give a sufficient criterion for the no-blur limit not to be a local minimizer. For the two-pixel family, the exact local loss-of-minimum threshold is w_local; Proposition 5 yields the sufficient bound w>max{w_local, l|b_+|^2(1+d)/(1+l)^2}, reducing to w>w_local when b_+=0. The new global switch occurs strictly earlier, at w_jump<w_local.

Wipf–Zhang arXiv:1305.2362, Sections 2, 3.5–3.6 and 4, treats a variational-Bayesian penalty coupling image sparsity, kernel norm and noise, rather than the specific independent determinant-prior quadratic variable-projection model.

Levin–Weiss–Durand–Freeman CVPR 2011 repository abstract covers approximate marginal-likelihood optimization; full PDF requested from MIT DSpace was inaccessible (HTTP 429). The abstract does not decide whether a full-text argument could subsume a scalar special case.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Proposition 5 is only a sufficient derivative sign criterion and can be more conservative if the constant Fourier component is nonzero. Even in the b_+=0 instance where its bound matches the exact local threshold, it does not classify the global optimum on the strict gap where the identity remains locally minimizing. The other models use distinct posterior/prior structures. The inaccessible plausible source is recorded as a residual risk, not a full-text NOT_COVERING assertion.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact global endpoint classification (including coexistence, unique barrier and auxiliary-scale transition) against Dworaczyk–Español Proposition 5 (local sufficient exclusion only), the prior general VB and marginal-likelihood methods, published mathematical-record comparisons and semantic published-finding corpus records. The source model and Fourier reduction are credited. No covering published result was identified in the inspected mathematical material; residual risk is explicit and does not amount to an unresolved decisive implication.
residual_risks: Older exact scalar Gaussian-marginal blur optimizations, especially uncatalogued marginal-likelihood literature, could imply the theorem under another parametrization; the searches do not prove absolute novelty.
The MIT 2011 primary PDF was inaccessible due to HTTP 429, and the 2024 SIAM paper was inspected only through its abstract; neither is falsely described as fully cleared.
No claim is made for dimensions larger than two or auxiliary scales beyond the strict first-order regime.

value.rationale: A determinant prior specifically motivated to avoid no-blur degeneration can instead force abrupt complete annihilation of the only nonconstant Fourier component, with a sharp open interval where local optimization still sees the wrong no-blur minimum. The two-site mass-preserving convolution is the smallest natural identifiable blur choice, and the exact global/local parameter thresholds provide a reproducible tuning and failure-mode benchmark.
